slides.title: Policy analysis: the 2024 refresh
text: Policies of similar topic were selected quarterly from DCT/divisions.
No set number of policies reviewed each quarter resulted in some drafting chairs having more than one policy.
Some uncertainty about how to complete an equity analysis. Few additional data sources identified. Completion rates very low.
Two policies selected for DCT/divisions every six months by equity/policy staff, based on importance and need and aligned with regular policy review.
Overview of the equity mindset and additional guidance for each new policy group.
The team includes a Division/DCT Health Equity Director, Policy Coordinator and data expert, in addition to the drafting chair/team.
Initial meeting: equitable service delivery, workplace inclusiveness, possible inequities/disparities, and useful internal and external data.
Additional drafting team meetings determined by each drafting chair.

slides.title: Cultivating an equity mindset
text: We can choose to create the space and support to act on our values.
Develop equity muscles and memory to override old habits and responses.
Learn to prime ourselves and others to take mindful action.

slides.title: Intent and impact
text: Intent is what we mean by our words and/or actions
Impact is how our words and/or actions are experienced, felt or understood by others

slides.title: Equity and the equity lens
text: Equity: The proactive and ongoing reinforcement of actions (policies, practices and attitudes) that re-distribute power by enhancing access, opportunities and outcomes.
Equity lens: A filter by which to guide one’s thoughts and actions with the intent to establish deliberate and continuous analyses of pervasive systemic and structural inequities.

slides.title: Equity analysis and affected communities
text: Equity analysis: A systemic process of examining the impact of decisions and actions to develop strategies that reduce and/or eliminate disparities and improve successes for communities experiencing inequities.

Communities experiencing inequities: For this policy, communities experiencing inequities refers to communities of color, multi-racial individuals, American Indians, veterans, LGBTQIA2S+ individuals, and individuals with disabilities.

slides.title: What the equity analysis tool offers
text: A systemic, methodical examination of impacts of decisions, policies, programs, practices, and budgets on  Communities experiencing inequities
Best used early in the process
To be conducted with a variety of perspectives
A way to ensure equity impacts are at the core of decision making – process improvement and prevention
To create space for traditionally marginalized communities to be incorporated in the process
An authentic, focused, and intentional effort to change, prevent, and dismantle institutional racism and discriminatory practice
To identify new options to remedy existing inequities (transformational change)

slides.title: Limits of the equity analysis tool
text: The Equity Analysis Tool Is Not:
A full stop of a process
Only applicable at the beginning; This process can be used to evaluate ongoing issues or programs
The only way to engage a variety of perspectives
Separate of existing processes or “add on”
A “checkbox” activity that does not consider creative ways to implement the recommendations (Transactional Changes)

slides.title: Drafting and leadership review
text: Drafting Chair Equity Review: 1. Assemble diverse Drafting Team for Analysis; 2. Engagement; 3. Evaluate Data; 4. Identify Benefits/Burdens and Mitigating Unintended Consequences; 5. Equity Impact Statement.
Leadership Equity Review: 6. Accountability, Evaluation, and Communication; 7. Alignment; 8. Sustainability.

slides.title: Convening a group
text: The Drafting Chair is tasked with assembling the team.
The team's diversity shapes the quality of the analysis itself and the quality of the process.
Does team adequately represent the organization?
Does team adequately represent the identities of people who will be impacted by the action(s) or decision(s)?
What perspectives does team have and what perspectives are still missing from the team?
How will the team engage missing perspectives?
Center shared-power: Include those at the table regardless of their title, but who may have a different perspective

slides.title: Practice with a policy
text: Facility Posting Requirements — Ambulatory Services. Page 1 of 3.
Issue date: October 3, 2023. Effective date: November 7, 2023. Policy number: 110-6000.
Policy: Ambulatory Services posts information for clients and employees as required by applicable licensing, regulatory and/or legal standards.

Authority: Minn. Stat. §245A.65 (Maltreatment of Vulnerable Adults); Minn. Stat. Sec.144.651 (Health Care Bill of Rights); Minn. Stat. Sec.144.121 (X-Ray Machines); Minn. Stat. Sec.150A.06 (Dentistry).
Applicability: Ambulatory Services, excluding the Facility Dental Clinics (MSOP, AMRTC and FS).
